show: 原创音乐剧《#0528》镜框版(出品人/监制 张轩豪,制作人 顾秋梦;导演/编舞 李勇,编剧 严栋瀚,作曲/编曲/作词 胡水;2026 年在天津大剧院歌剧厅、上海星空间28号等地演出的中国原创音乐剧)。⚠ 请只描述【上面这一部制作】的剧情;如果找不到这部戏的资料,请直接说明找不到,【不要用同名或题材相近的其他作品】(小说、电影、电视剧、其他音乐剧或戏曲)的剧情来代替,也不要凭剧名推测
synopsis:
In New York’s room 0528, Eggy arrives carrying a fierce ambition to become a musical-theatre performer and the exhaustion of one setback too many. The cheap apartment seems at first to offer only a place to regroup, but it is already occupied by Doris and Brandon, two aspiring actors whose presence is impossible to explain: thirteen years earlier, an accidental fire left them gravely injured, and they became ghosts unable to leave the room. Their first encounters are prickly and comic, as Eggy resists the intrusions of these unwanted housemates while Doris and Brandon bristle at the newcomer disrupting the small world they have preserved for years.

As the three are forced to share the apartment, their mutual suspicion gives way to companionship. Eggy’s struggles to find a place onstage echo Doris and Brandon’s own unfinished hopes, and the room gradually becomes a refuge where disappointments can be voiced rather than concealed. The framed-stage version also looks back to Doris and Brandon’s earlier life: they meet and grow close in New Orleans, then travel to New York together, sustained by a shared dream of Broadway. Their history reveals both the warmth of their bond and the ambitions that the fire abruptly interrupted.

Eggy’s presence changes what 0528 means to them. Encouraged by Doris and Brandon, Eggy confronts fear, persists through professional rejection, and moves toward the stage rather than retreating from it. In return, watching Eggy continue the journey they could not complete lets Doris and Brandon revisit their old regrets without being consumed by them. The three do not erase one another’s losses; instead, they help transform an apartment defined by confinement into a temporary home from which each can move forward.

The musical centres on dreams, missed chances, and the courage to keep pursuing a calling after failure. It suggests that love for the stage can be passed on, while companionship can make it possible to release an unfinished past and accept an imperfect life.

show: 音乐剧《Borderline-边界线》中文版(韩国 WELCOMEFUNNY 原版制作,原版总制作人 YOU HWAN WOONG,编剧 YUMIN,作曲 PARK JIYOUNG;中方出品/制作 缪时客,执行制作厂牌 M²,导演 Tobias Weis,剧本翻译 胡楚浩/Dylan Goike,韩语校对 静国玲;2026 年在上海长江剧场·红匣子演出。🚨 不是 Benjamin Velez 作曲、Aryanna Garber 编剧的那部美国原创音乐喜剧《BORDERLINE》,也不是任何以边缘型人格障碍(BPD)为题材的作品——那是同名的另一部戏,请勿混淆)。⚠ 请只描述【上面这一部制作】的剧情;如果找不到这部戏的资料,请直接说明找不到,【不要用同名或题材相近的其他作品】(小说、电影、电视剧、其他音乐剧或戏曲)的剧情来代替,也不要凭剧名推测
synopsis:
July reports to a newly assigned office at the headquarters of Borderline, a clandestine company that sells death exclusively to people judged beyond redemption. As a child, July was saved by an unnamed Borderline employee, and that encounter became an enduring ideal: joining the organisation means not merely becoming a killer, but helping to deliver a form of justice that the city has abandoned. Eager to prove worthy of that mission, July arrives prepared to work by the book and to make a difference.

The new assignment, however, comes with Jun as a partner. Jun has the worst record in the office and refuses to cooperate with the committed newcomer. His indifference and resistance leave July struggling to understand both the job and the moral certainty that once seemed so clear. February, their superior and Jun’s longtime friend, offers a troubling explanation. Jun was once a fearsome operative whose name made the city’s evildoers tremble; something in his past has since turned him into a man convinced that no individual can change anything.

Caught between July’s faith in a righteous purpose, Jun’s exhausted disillusionment, and February’s uncompromising view that weakness and hypocrisy cannot cleanse a corrupt world, the three operatives confront the line between punishment and justice. Their work forces them to decide who has the authority to condemn another person—and whether killing the worst people can truly repair the conditions that produced them.

At its core, the musical examines justice in a city where formal morality has failed, asking whether violence can ever become an ethical remedy. It also sets youthful idealism against experience, cynicism, and the dangerous appeal of absolute certainty.

synopsis:
In postwar Amsterdam, Lieutenant Piller is ordered to take charge of a sealed gallery and uncover the truth behind an extraordinary wartime transaction. Its proprietor, the art dealer Han van Meegeren, stands accused of having sold a painting of immense national importance to Hermann Göring, a leading Nazi official. What begins as an administrative investigation swiftly becomes a public reckoning: Professor Martin examines the work and declares that its provenance provides damning proof of van Meegeren’s collaboration and treason.

As the case attracts worldwide attention, van Meegeren is confronted with the prospect of execution. The interrogations close in on the dealer’s actions during the occupation, asking whether the painting’s sale was an act of betrayal, greed, survival, or something less easily named. Piller must work through the gallery’s confiscated remnants and the competing accounts surrounding the work, while Martin’s expert judgment gives the accusation its decisive force. The trial turns van Meegeren into a figure onto whom a wounded nation projects its outrage: a man apparently responsible for placing a Dutch cultural treasure in the hands of the enemy. With the noose of a treason conviction tightening, the central question becomes not merely what was sold, but what van Meegeren truly did—and why.

The musical examines the unstable boundary between artistic authority and deception, and between public condemnation and private truth. It also asks how people assign guilt after war, when patriotism, profit, shame, and the urge for self-preservation can become impossible to separate.

synopsis:
In 1930s Beijing, three young people of sharply different temperaments cross paths amid a country unsettled by war and social upheaval. Drawn together by circumstance, they begin travelling the same difficult road, forming a bond that gives each of them a measure of courage and companionship. Their encounters are not presented as the deeds of celebrated heroes, but as the lived experience of ordinary people whose choices acquire weight in an age that continually tests them.

As the three grow closer, they are forced to confront the distance between their hopes and the world as it is. Personal ambitions, loyalty to one another, and the pressure to compromise collide as reality repeatedly challenges the ideals they want to preserve. Moments of warmth and humour emerge from their companionship, yet the surrounding turmoil makes clear that affection alone cannot shield them from loss, uncertainty, or the consequences of their decisions. Each must decide whether to retreat into self-protection or to keep faith with a future that remains difficult to see.

Their shared journey becomes a process of growing up: learning what idealism costs, recognising the fragility of individual lives in the current of history, and discovering that even limited acts of persistence can matter. Rather than resolving the era’s vast conflicts, the story locates its emotional force in the three youths’ effort to remain connected and to protect what they believe in while the world changes around them. The production’s public description identifies 1930s Beijing and this trio’s meeting, companionship, and struggle between ideals and reality as its central narrative frame.

The musical centres on idealism under pressure, friendship forged in instability, and the dignity of small people facing overwhelming historical forces. It suggests that courage need not mean changing the whole world: it can also mean refusing to abandon one’s convictions or companions.
